# arctic-glass

Cold, light, airy, translucent — panels read as frosted/dark glass floating
with real depth over a sparse, icy wallpaper, not as "monochrome with a
blue tint." Deep blue-tinted blacks and cool grays carry the whole UI; a
single controlled ice-blue/cyan accent shows up only on the active border
and selection — never spread across the palette.

## Palette

| Token | Hex | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | `#0A0F16` | app/wallpaper base, deepest blue-black |
| `background_alt` | `#0D141C` | secondary background surfaces |
| `surface` | `#121B25` | panel/card glass fill (Rofi surface, SwayNC surface) |
| `surface_alt` | `#1A2530` | raised surface variant, inactive tabs |
| `foreground` | `#E8F0F5` | primary text — cool white, not pure white |
| `foreground_strong` | `#FFFFFF` | emphasis text (clock, selected row) |
| `muted` | `#8CA0AF` | secondary text, inactive tab labels |
| `subtle` | `#3D4C58` | dividers, selection background, least prominent text |
| `border_inactive` | `#2A3A46` | unfocused window/panel border |
| `border_active` / `accent` | `#7FD8E8` | focused window border, cursor, selection accent — the *only* saturated color in the theme |

## Structurally different from monochrome

Monochrome: `border_size=1, gaps_in=8, gaps_out=16, rounding=9,
rounding_power=4, blur_size=6, blur_passes=2, active_opacity=1.0,
inactive_opacity=0.97`.

arctic-glass:

- **Border**: `border_size=1` (kept thin/hairline — a soft ice-blue line,
  not a frame).
- **Gaps**: `gaps_in=10, gaps_out=20` — more breathing room than
  monochrome's 8/16, so panels read as floating rather than tiled.
- **Rounding**: `rounding=14` (vs. 9) with `rounding_power=3` (vs. 4) —
  larger *and* rounder corners (closer to a true circle than monochrome's
  squircle), which suits a glass panel's softness.
- **Blur**: `blur_size=10, blur_passes=4` (vs. 6/2) — substantially more
  blur so glass genuinely separates from what's behind it. Also
  `blur_brightness=1.06` (vs. monochrome's dimming `0.9`) and
  `blur_vibrancy=0.15`/`blur_vibrancy_darkness=0.2` (vs. monochrome's
  `0`/`0`) so the cool wallpaper hues actually bleed through the frost
  instead of graying out.
- **Opacity**: `active_opacity=0.92, inactive_opacity=0.82` (vs. 1.0/0.97)
  — visibly more transparent, so windows read as glass, not solid slabs.
- **Component alpha**: Waybar `bar_bg` alpha `0.62` (vs. monochrome's
  `0.8`); Rofi `background`/`surface` alpha `0xB8`/`0xCC` ≈ `0.72`/`0.80`
  (vs. `0xD6`/`0xE8` ≈ `0.84`/`0.91`); SwayNC `bg` alpha `0.62` (vs.
  `0.8`) — all lower than monochrome's, so the heavier compositor blur
  above has real translucency to show through, while staying legible.

## Wallpaper pack

Generated by `scripts/dev/generate_wallpaper_arctic_glass.py`, standard
library only, deterministic per-variant seed. Canonical
`wallpapers/arctic-glass.png` is a byte-identical copy of `shard`.

- **shard** (default) — large dark blue-glass planes on long diagonals, a
  soft off-center glow, one or two thin ice-blue cuts. Architectural, not
  busy.
- **horizon** — a sparse perspective floor converging on a glowing
  vanishing point, with a single strong ice-blue horizon line. Cold,
  spacious, restrained.
- **drift** — the quietest variant: a few soft cold glows and a scatter of
  tiny particles suspended in near-black space, one crisp accent line.
- **aurora** — broad, gently-angled cold glow bands low in the frame over
  a near-black blue field, anchored by a thin baseline and a single
  ice-blue accent line.

All four are ≥1920×1080, truecolor RGB, and use arctic-glass's real
cool-blue palette (not grayscale) while keeping saturation/contrast
tasteful per the visual brief.

## Motion — "glide"

Overrides `motion` in `hypr.lua`; every spring sits at damping ratio
~0.90–0.95 (near the high end monochrome's own range tops out at, e.g.
window ~0.88) so nothing overshoots more than a hair and nothing bounces
— it just settles. Speeds are slightly longer than monochrome's so it
reads as floaty/premium rather than instantaneous, without feeling laggy:

| Spring | stiffness | damping | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| window | 220 | 28 | ~0.944 |
| workspace | 190 | 26 | ~0.943 |
| layer | 230 | 28 | ~0.923 |
| special_workspace | 190 | 25 | ~0.907 |

Speeds (deciseconds): `windows=1.9` (mono 1.6), `windows_in=2.1` (1.8),
`windows_out=1.3` (1.2), `windows_move=0.9` (unchanged — drag/resize stays
1:1 with input), `layers_in=1.8` (1.5), `layers_out=1.2` (1.1),
`fade_in=1.15` (1.0), `fade_out=0.9` (0.8), `workspaces=2.3` (2.0),
`special_workspace=2.3` (2.0), `border=0.85` (0.8).

Styles: `windows_popin="popin 96%"` (softer/less shrink than mono's 94%),
`workspaces="slidefade 10%"` and `special_workspace="slidefadevert 8%"`
(smaller displacement than mono's 15%/12% — a hint of drift, not a slide).

## Manual verification (real hardware only)

Everything below passed static checks (`tests/check_all_themes.py`,
`tests/run_tests.sh`, JSON/CSS structure, PNG decoding) but needs eyes on
the actual target machine (Hyprland 0.56.2 / Wayland / 1920x1080@75Hz) to
confirm it feels/looks right — this environment has no Hyprland/lua/
Waybar/Rofi/SwayNC/Kitty binaries to run any of this live:

```sh
git pull && ./apply.sh
hyprctl configerrors   # expect: clean
```

- **Glass depth**: focused/unfocused windows should visibly show blurred
  wallpaper through them (`active_opacity=0.92`/`inactive_opacity=0.82`,
  `blur_size=10`/`blur_passes=4`) — check this isn't so transparent that
  text becomes hard to read over a busy wallpaper region.
- **Rounding**: corners should look distinctly larger and rounder than
  monochrome's, closer to a circle than a squircle.
- **Windows**: opening should read as a soft, slightly floaty
  materialize with no visible bounce (`popin 96%` on the window spring,
  damping ratio ~0.94); closing quicker and clean. Drag/resize should
  still track the cursor with zero perceptible lag.
- **Workspaces** (`SUPER+1..0`): a short, gentle slide+fade — noticeably
  softer/smaller displacement than monochrome, but not sluggish.
- **Special workspace** (`SUPER+S`): a touch livelier than a normal
  workspace switch (ratio ~0.91 vs ~0.94), still no obvious bounce.
- **Rofi** (`SUPER+R`): should pop in centered as a deep, translucent
  glass panel — confirm the lower alpha (`0xB8`/`0xCC`) still reads as
  unmistakably a panel, not washed out or illegible against a bright
  wallpaper region.
- **Waybar**: bar should read as clearly translucent (alpha `0.62`) with
  real blur behind it, not a flat dark strip.
- **SwayNC**: control-center panel should feel refined and deep, not
  rough/flat — check the ice-blue accent shows only on interactive
  elements, not as a wash across the whole panel.
- **Kitty**: cool palette should look good at the shared 0.82 background
  opacity over each wallpaper variant, especially `shard`/`horizon`.
- **Brave**: install `themes/arctic-glass/brave/manifest.json` as an
  unpacked theme and confirm frame/toolbar/omnibox/tabs/NTP all read as
  cool dark-blue, matching the rest of the desktop.
- **Hyprlock**: confirm the lock screen's blur/labels/input-field read as
  the same cool-glass identity as the rest of the theme.
